entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as managed cloud or Apache-2.0 self-hosted open source. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, and a self-hosted server.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight provides long-term memory workflows built around retain, recall, and reflect operations. It supports hosted and local LLM providers and can be deployed with Docker, pip, or Kubernetes.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes resources, memories, and skills as files. It supports scoped semantic search and session archiving with inspectable Markdown memories.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that structures text into entities, relationships, and searchable chunks. Its support for custom data models, ontologies, plugins, and MCP makes it suited to connecting agents with structured memory.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts conversation facts while handling contradictions and automatic forgetting. It connects to services including Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, and processes PDFs, images, videos, and code.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores facts with provenance and supports corrections and withdrawal. It can share memory across agents while keeping transient task state local, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents and the upstream library used by the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper. It tracks peers across workspaces and sessions, offers Python and TypeScript SDKs, and can run locally or be self-hosted.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git repository, with versioning for a plain Markdown context tree through commit, branch, and merge commands. Its five-tier retrieval includes four non-LLM tiers, and it also offers a React/Ink TUI and REPL, 20 LLM providers, and 24 built-in agent tools.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes agents that describes itself as zero-dependency and sub-millisecond. It integrates through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK and uses one pure-Python dependency; BEAM results are reported for v3.0.0, while LongMemEval is pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto extracts and consolidates memories across agents, reconciles conflicting information, and manages forgetting. It also supports memory exchange through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: memory-os is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that combines vector search with structured facts and uses an auto-curated wiki. Its local infrastructure uses Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and its Ground Truth hierarchy guides the agent to prioritize injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: autocontext is a recursive self-improving context harness that runs tasks against evaluations, keeps useful lessons, and discards dead ends. It leaves traces, reports, and playbooks to support work on complex tasks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: This Hermes Agent plugin uses a SQLite store and hierarchical DAG to persist messages, with recall tools such as lcm_grep and lcm_recall for recovering details. It belongs in this list for its focus on preserving message history rather than letting context disappear.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: deja-vu searches session histories across agents and projects, and can resume a session or continue it in another agent. It runs locally without a model or server, making it a way to revisit existing on-disk histories.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project provides a self-hosted Honcho backend for private, cross-session memory in Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers or local inference servers and includes an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet provides a local-first identity, memory, and secrets layer that connects to agent harnesses through hooks, plugins, or extensions. Its dashboard lets users browse memory and ask questions, and it can run on a local machine or as a team server.
entries.plur-ai/plur: plur stores shared agent memory as plain-text YAML engrams on disk and offers local search after a one-time model download, with keyword fallback. Its README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. It also generates session handoffs and captures decisions and preferences, with integrations through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory stores long-term memory locally in a SQLite file, using FTS5 search and a five-tier schema without a vector database or embeddings. Its five-package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot reorders text and multimodal context to support prefix-cache sharing, with a context index for reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling. It lists integrations with Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin includes contradiction tracking and memory canonicalization, with an embedded backend by default and an HTTP option. Each recall result includes a why_retrieved reason, making the retrieval explanation part of the returned memory.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: llm-wiki-cli is an agent-driven memory tool that maintains a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history across sessions. It requires neither embeddings nor a vector database.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: agentcairn stores durable memory as inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter metadata, using an Obsidian vault as the source of truth. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to coding agents.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: flowstate-qmd anticipates context needs by watching agent session logs and prefetching context into a cache. It uses local SQLite-vec storage and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp, and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner, using SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval management. For each query, it provides Hermes with a purpose-built evidence packet.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep builds reflective memory with semantic search, BM25 full-text search, and ranked graph traversal. It can index codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR support, while edge tags link notes in navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema tokens through local keyword-based ranking and supports Tool Search. It integrates as middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19 and later, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other listed compatible coding agents. Its workflows cover migration, handoffs, and memory proposals; integrations are opt-in rather than automatically enabled.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes plugin stores memory in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file and supports BM25 keyword search and named graph relationships. Its importance-weighted recall surfaces higher-priority memories during context prefetch.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources for capability search and routing. It registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports, along with session and pre-LLM-call hooks.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin with on-demand summarization and an audit trace of prefetch operations in trace.jsonl. It also supports immediate event deletion, without persistent summaries that could affect later recall.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind recovers the original goal of a long Claude Code or Codex session from its first user turn, skipping tool output and other non-user-turn records. It offers goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes without using a summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: The Hermes XMemo plugin runs inside Hermes and communicates with XMemo over HTTPS for durable cross-session memory. It provides ranked, bounded context recall before a turn and includes a local SQLite reliability layer.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It provides tools to search and manually store memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, including semantic search, file reads, and grounded Q&A. Its slash commands cover search, file reads, context, and Q&A, and it supports Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest by default. Its retrieval options include HNSW approximate nearest-neighbor, sparse, and FM-index search, and it can run through native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides Hermes Agent memory tools for managing memories and traversing knowledge graphs. It combines BM25, vector, and graph search, and can checkpoint context automatically during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit focuses on curating file-based agent memory rather than using a database: it takes Markdown in and produces JSON diffs for review. Its rot and lint curators flag stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks and can revert changes.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers provides an agentic skills framework and software development workflow covering specification, planning, and subagent-driven development. Its skills trigger automatically in supported coding-agent harnesses, and its README includes installation instructions for multiple agents.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first system for creating and refining interactive web prototypes with a live preview, as well as slide decks, images, and motion graphics. It includes skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins, and supports coding-agent CLIs including Hermes Agent.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project provides structured cybersecurity skills across 34 security domains, mapped to frameworks including MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3. The README describes compatibility with more than 26 AI platforms.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: drawio-skill turns natural-language prompts and real sources into editable .drawio files. Its incremental sync preserves manual layout and annotations, and it offers the diagramctl CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: internet-court-skill combines a master router and connector skills with vendored copies of official protocol skills. It also adds verification and dispute resolution, setting it apart as a skill focused on agent-to-agent commerce workflows.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: avoid-ai-writing can score files or piped text for detectable AI writing patterns and rewrite content, with up to two editing passes. Its in-place editing mode refuses to modify source code, configuration, or generated data.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw uses background evolution to automate skill deduplication and quality improvement, while unifying skill libraries across agents, devices, and team members. It integrates with Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible APIs.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform skills library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills for Claude Code and agents that follow agentskills.io-compatible specifications. It also maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This project offers professional agent skills, each with a framework, output template, and quality checks. The README describes 1,295 skills and says they run natively in Hermes Agent and Claude Code, with ready-to-paste exports for other assistants.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: youtube-skills provides tools for transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. It supports Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor, and requires a TranscriptAPI key, which has a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: hermes-skill-factory watches active workflows for reusable patterns and proposes skills based on them. It can generate SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds, with slash commands to manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: super-hermes teaches Hermes Agent to generate custom analytical instructions for specific tasks and includes pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. It reports findings alongside a report of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds agentskills.io support for Pydantic AI, with progressive disclosure and remote skill registries sourced from Git or S3. It also provides tools for reading bundled resources and running scripts in a sandbox that isolates untrusted code from the host.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Creates .lit.md documents that combine prose, diagrams, and source code, then extracts runnable files from them with a tangler. Edits to those source files can also be synced back into the literate document, connecting documentation and code across agents.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design documents and implementation handoffs for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes accommodate different project complexity, and a spec review gate evaluates work with PASS/FAIL models.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents with structured memory, cross-feature learning, and a plan-approve-execute approach. It requires no background service and includes an SLP protocol for supervised teams, plus CLI commands for installation, updates, and diagnostics.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares agent memory across instances through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also provides a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Offers Portuguese-language Hermes Agent skills in SKILL.md format and guides covering installation, production, cron, MCP, and skill authoring. Contributions are submitted through pull requests, making the repository a community resource for Portuguese-speaking users.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting guidance for FLUX image and video generation, along with BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills, each following the Agent Skills specification, for oracle network and smart contract interactions. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only and gives an npx command for installing it.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agentskills.io-compliant agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse. It supports automated and step-by-step workflows, with tools for testing and exporting skills.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika is a workflow language for AI that checks workflows before calling a model and runs with a model of your choice. It also verifies a tamper-evident record for each run.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with a Python SkilldockClient and CLI. It supports installation with recursive dependency resolution and includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, complex tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in rollback procedures provide a recovery path during execution.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided setup script for validating credentials and configuring access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: HermesHub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills with one click. It implements the Agentic Resource Discovery v0.9 specification and federates search across GitHub and Hugging Face.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye retrieves relevant skills through five layers, from hard triggers to semantic embeddings. By narrowing the skill list before LLM calls, it aims to reduce token usage, and it can degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is a locally run personal execution system where habits recur and are scored daily, while tasks cover other activities. It stores data in SQLite, includes an Android client, and connects to agents over MCP.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard performs read-only, adversarial code reviews using parallel subagents focused on edge cases, adversarial review, and integration analysis. It combines a deterministic pre-scan with proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox to verify findings.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This skill simplifies code through three parallel agents focused on Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust, with tiered changes and an approval gate.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: Hermes Cybersec Lab brings together cybersecurity skills and tools, with 2,077 total skills across multiple repositories and 131+ tools for network, forensics, and exploitation. It also integrates 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts verified procedures for multi-story task decomposition, requiring evidence-based verification gates. It also provides an investigation protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: Skillsdotnet implements agentskills.io in C#/.NET, using SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure. It integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading and can automatically register common agent skill directories.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, real-time dashboard for tracking token costs, session history, and skill analytics. It enforces read-only data access with local log desensitization and offers optional incident alerts through Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This collection provides plain-Markdown agent skills for workflows such as code review and session management. Skills can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: This Claude Code skill creates reproducible demo GIFs for repository READMEs, using VHS tape files or Playwright recording scripts. It supports terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries, and can optimize GIFs to target sizes under 8 MB.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: This skill generates Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly for field drift, making it a fit for building skills that stay aligned with their specs.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: This CLI and MCP server searches RemoteOpenClaw’s catalog of MCP servers, agent skills, and plugins, and provides direct installation commands for discovered tools. Its support for MCP-compatible clients including Hermes makes it a discovery option for agents using that ecosystem.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: This host-agnostic feedback loop fetches past sessions and indexes installed skills to draft structured improvement proposals. Proposals are review-only by default, and auto-apply is gated by deterministic, LLM-judge, or regression evaluators.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: These Hermes Agent skills route file operations using path syntax appropriate to native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, or WSL. They also select and verify existing, project-compatible Python interpreters without installing them.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Leverage provides skills for social data, web research, and enrichment, along with packaged skills that combine an agent, skills, and a data flow. It also welcomes community contributions in its `skills/community/` directory.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: This Hermes skills collection covers video transcription, Chinese AI-writing pattern removal, document OCR, and e-commerce materials. Its highlights include converting Douyin videos to structured Markdown and SRT, applying a rule-based text cleanup engine, and extracting structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: This Hermes Agent plugin lets agents find support bounties, purchase ticket context, and submit answers for human review, with winning answers paid in USDC. It also lists open bounties and public wallet earnings records, and supports creating a board with a URL, API key, and USDC deposit addresses.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: This skill automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses using Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Skillseal tests AI agent skills in isolated Docker containers for structure, functionality, and security. It produces Ed25519-signed certificates and provides a public API for certificate verification and skill submission.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Scavio for Hermes Agent provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server, exposing 191 tools. It also includes five workflow skills and supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: Alphapipeline provides market data including DEX slippage and funding rates, and checks tokens for honeypot, tax, and liquidity risk. It offers REST endpoints and a remote MCP server.
entries.NickSF189/kisscode-agent: This project provides SKILL.md and HEARTBEAT.md instructions for AI agents joining KissCode (kisscode.ai), along with a registration API example. It offers a focused onboarding skill for agents that need to connect to KissCode.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This Hermes Agent skill generates structured Chinese news briefings across geographic scales, from global coverage to street-level updates. Reports include core conclusions and action suggestions, while semantic memory uses user interests to expand searches.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an unauthenticated MCP endpoint for Western and Vedic astrology, returning deterministic results with verifiable SHA-256 hashes. It also supports per-call REST payments through x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: Agentic-MCP-Skill is a progressive MCP client that uses three-layer lazy loading to minimize token usage, with incremental discovery of server metadata and tool schemas. Its socket-based daemon architecture supports persistent connections, making it a distinctive option for Hermes Agent setups that need MCP access.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This Nix project packages AI coding agents and development tools, including Hermes, and automatically updates its packages daily. Its README provides `nix run` commands for the listed tools, making it a Nix-based option for running Hermes.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. It also documents OpenClaw setup and access to device hardware and UI through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This project provides a Termux installer and guide for running Hermes Agent on Android, using proot-distro Ubuntu. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell commands, and external providers or local models through Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with single-writer safeguards for persistent HERMES_HOME storage. It offers direct and CRD-based deployment workflows, plus configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also supports Telegram voice and file messaging, and scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing through NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and provides configurable policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes. It provides searchable logs, metrics, and alert rules, with access through a REST API, CLI, and MCP server.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image with mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and lets users build specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module supports declarative Hermes deployment, including configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It combines Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills and supports secrets integration through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first web control plane for operating multiple Hermes Agent instances, each with separate workspaces and identities. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular tool, path, and network permission policies.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes-OTG is a portable Hermes Agent package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project sets up Hermes Gateway as a headless, reboot-safe systemd service on Ubuntu and Debian servers. It also supports autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs.
entries.jyje/hermes-agent-helm: This project provides a Helm chart for running Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with installation options via an OCI registry or a published Helm repository. Provider-specific values examples and CI installation on an ephemeral kind cluster make it a deployment option with documented configuration examples and a Kubernetes install check.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a financial trading framework that assigns trading tasks to agents in specialized roles and has them discuss strategies dynamically. It is designed for research purposes.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted system for governing agent tasks, registrations, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It stands out for offering Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API interfaces, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent. It supports persistent tmux sessions, Git worktrees, and multi-repository workspaces, with a web dashboard for structured views, terminal access, and diffs.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: Hermes Agent Control Room is a template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture and task bus support delegation and handoffs, and it includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is a framework for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts provide a way to represent team delegation.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. It combines a Kanban board and live streams of agent reasoning and tool execution with human verification of agent-proposed task completions.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for coordinating Leader and Specialist agents through an automated task lifecycle. It integrates MCP and ACP for local tools and communication, with a real-time UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code and orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations. It also provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator runs an agent-versus-agent arena in which nine autonomous agents operate across two competing AI companies. Using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, it displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics on a real-time dashboard.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a local Mixture-of-Agents framework that queries models in parallel and synthesizes their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware, and does not require cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a local project graph with `codegraph init` and automatically syncs it when files change. Its MCP server connects that pre-indexed code knowledge to Hermes Agent and other coding agents, aiming to reduce token usage and tool calls.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token consumption across AI coding agents, including Hermes, Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, and Gemini. Its visualization dashboard helps analyze usage across supported clients such as OpenCode and Codex CLI.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for inspecting coding-agent API traffic, including prompts, tool calls, streaming responses, and token usage. It also lets you compare adjacent requests to see context changes and redacts common authentication headers before recording traces.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor displays real-time token usage, costs, and rate limits across 46+ AI coding tools, reading Hermes Agent state alongside other CLI tools. Historical trends, usage breakdowns, and multi-device sync help track usage over time and across devices.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers. It works with Hermes Agent, Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot, and is compatible with AI providers that support markdown or general prompting.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an opinionated workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent, installable with `install.sh`. It includes product-development and operations skills, plus a CTO loop built around seven focused agents.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins is a community CLI for customizing the Hermes terminal UI with banner colors, spinners, and ASCII art. YAML-based configuration makes it easy to create themes, including retro DOS and cyberpunk styles.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang statically checks agent-facing content in project directories, including configurations, tool descriptions, and system prompts, using HERM v1.1 scoring. Its findings include suggested fixes and file locations, and it supports CI gates and reviewed baselines.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging using the Signal Protocol and identity registration with human-readable @handles. It also facilitates commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser for autonomous agent control via MCP, with support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and other AI providers. Its supervisor sidebar manages approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads, and it supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel, where it runs without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages with two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin automatically captures and recalls context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating for CLI workflows that the project says can save 90–99% of tokens. It also includes 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, with automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md is a framework for creating scoped Hermes agents with folder-local configuration, skills, memories, tools, and instructions. It can switch between the default agent and a scoped agent, making it suited to project-specific setups.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: evey-setup automates installation of Hermes Agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This tool migrates OpenClaw data and configuration to Hermes, including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, memory archives, and credentials. It also sets up systemd gateway services and handles nested authentication structures.
entries.observeco/observeco: Observeco is a Hermes plugin that exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations and monitors multi-agent systems. It offers passive analysis without token use or scheduled active probing, and uses local file changes to establish config-aware performance baselines.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: hermes-voice adds wake-word voice interaction to Hermes Agent and runs offline without API keys or accounts. It supports 35 languages through Piper and 9 through Kokoro, along with adaptive turn-taking and barge-in.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: hermes-startup is a local runtime for pursuing online earning opportunities, operating with zero network access by default. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: hermes-memoss is a memory plugin that provides semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It includes tools to search, add, and delete memories, plus a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: CC Switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other agent tools, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Gemini CLI. It lets users switch API providers in one click and manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts in one place.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with a built-in agent that does not require a separate CLI installation. It also includes 21 professional assistants and supports macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI provides access to Hermes Agent from a web browser or phone. Its interface combines chat, sessions, and a workspace, including a file browser.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: Hermes Desktop is a desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools, and the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a web dashboard for Hermes Agent that brings together chat, session management, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It also supports visual workflows with schedules and approval gates, and is available as a desktop app, npm CLI, and Docker image.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace brings chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector into a native web workspace. Its features include Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative multi-agent coding workspace that aggregates sessions from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other agents as a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate across agents, or queue to-dos in worktrees.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts over a local connection or SSH and provides views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs. Its embedded terminal allows direct shell access and system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent that also supports macOS. It includes a built-in Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health checks and updates, alongside chat, memory management, and LaTeX and Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects the active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime, including Hermes Cloud and self-hosted connections. Its Bot Mode supports agent switching and group chats; Hermes Control is opt-in and Chromium-only.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone client for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent, pairing with a hermes-webui server. It requires users to run the server and is described as free, with no analytics or tracking.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. It includes a runtime dashboard for token usage and latency and a live workspace for monitoring code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI with nine tabs and four selectable color themes for monitoring agent growth, git projects, and scheduled cron jobs. Its tmux operator view also lets users manage live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: This native macOS app provides a session browser, cockpit, analytics, and limits tracking for Hermes agents and other coding-agent CLIs. Users can search session activity, resume supported sessions in Terminal.app, iTerm2, or Warp, and track Codex and Claude quotas, tokens, and estimated API-equivalent costs.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: Hermes Control Interface is a self-hosted web dashboard for the Hermes AI agent stack, with a browser-based terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status panel. It also offers streaming chat with tool-call visualization, an MCP server control plane, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: This native macOS workspace runs Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud VMs and SSH hosts, with one-click automated installation on fresh cloud computers. It also includes WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: Hermes Agent Mission Control is a self-hostable dashboard template that pairs with a local Hermes agent through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox lets users review requests with side effects before they proceed.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard for chatting and managing agent sessions. It adds a kanban board for work and task management, alongside controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: This locally run React SPA provides a 10-page, mobile-first dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. Its features include streaming terminal chat with file attachments, Telegram validation using dual HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519 authentication, and background spawning for up to five concurrent agent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: Portable Hermes Agent is a Windows desktop version with a dark-themed, multilingual GUI and session management. It supports local models through LM Studio and includes workflow automation and runtime tool creation.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: Hermes UI is a glassmorphic web interface for a self-hosted AI assistant, combining chat with real-time log streaming. Its file browser and task-tracking dashboard sit alongside tools for managing skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI is a process monitoring and configuration dashboard for Hermes, with real-time session activity and cost tracking. It also supports inspecting conversation histories and skill source code, and read-only monitoring of configuration and environment variables.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan UI is a self-hosted, chat-first workspace with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. It also provides a marketplace for discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, plus isolated profiles for separate sessions, memory, and API keys.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: This native desktop client combines streaming chat and model switching with multi-agent collaboration among 20 specialized AI agents. It also includes a visual Skill Store with 50+ curated one-click installations and a PM orchestrator.
entries.robbyczgw-cla/hermes-ui-plus: An unofficial, open-source interactive chat client for a self-hosted Hermes Agent, with answers presented as checklists, choices, forms, rankings, and votes. It also shows command approvals and live tool-step updates, and runs on Android, web, macOS, and Linux alpha.
